Q1.question: Performance design (paste-parse hot path)
Q1.binding: Pure-function module with typed ParseResult; one-pass pointer arithmetic on the input string; 200-item cap; segment-isolation rule restated inline in every test

Q2.question: Security design (per-action audit append)
Q2.binding: Typed appendAudit helper imported from U1's AuditService; called BEFORE the DB write; the B2 R2.1 gate asserts the helper is called

Q3.question: Code quality design (status enum + bucket math)
Q3.binding: Discriminated string-literal union with exhaustive switch + never-asserted default; module-level bucket constants restated inline in every test

Q4.question: Reliability design (order hot path)
Q4.binding: Single synchronous path with typed appendAudit helper + DB-level audit-immutability; one DB transaction per mutation; free-tier managed-DB daily snapshot as the recovery point

Q5.question: Observability design (deferred-input logging)
Q5.binding: Module-level deferred_input_invoked log event with typed shape; the log line is the audit-log row shape (a stable contract); the R2.5 gate asserts the log line shape

Q6.question: Logical components (failure domain mapping)
Q6.binding: Orders unit is one failure domain; paste-parse is the highest-risk surface; the 3 deferred input mode placeholders are isolated (their failure is the deferred reason, not a crash)

Q7.question: Scalability design (list size + paste-parse cap)
Q7.binding: Cursor-based pagination (page size 50, max 1 000 orders rendered) + client-side size cap on paste-parse (200 items); status-bucket math computed on the rendered page, not the full list
